title: The Law of Least Effort
coreMove: Redesign the friction around a behavior so the desired action becomes the path of least resistance and the undesired action takes one extra step.

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift ICU nurse trying to chart patient notes in real time instead of at the end of a twelve-hour shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician whose documentation backlog is eating her breaks
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether charting accuracy slips because notes get written from memory at 6am
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse moves the charting tablet from the nurses' station to a wheeled cart that follows her, and refuses to add any motivational reminder — only the physical relocation

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher trying to get a sixteen-year-old cellist to practice on weeknights
exampleSpecs.audience: a music teacher coaching a student who keeps saying she 'didn't have time'
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the student keeps her chair before regional auditions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher walks the student through the actual seconds between walking in the door and bow on string, and they cut three steps by leaving the cello unzipped on a stand by the couch

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance tax preparer who keeps reopening Twitter between client returns during the March crunch
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed worker losing two billable hours a day to phone-checking
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she finishes the season without taking on debt to cover rent in April
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses between deleting the app, logging out each time, or putting the phone in a drawer across the room — and reasons explicitly about which adds the most friction without depending on willpower

exampleSpecs.domain: a community garden coordinator trying to get volunteers to water plots on Saturday mornings
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator who has begged, emailed, and guilted with no result
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether half the summer crop dies in a July heat wave
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator stops sending reminder emails and instead coils the hose at the gate with a chalkboard listing three plots; volunteer turnout doubles without a single new message sent

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired structural engineer trying to walk thirty minutes a day after a knee replacement
exampleSpecs.audience: a 68-year-old man whose physical therapist set a non-negotiable daily walk
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether his recovery stalls and he loses the ability to climb to his second-floor bedroom
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he notices that on the days he walks, his sneakers were already by the front door — and on the days he doesn't, they were in the hall closet behind the vacuum

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook prepping mise en place for a Friday dinner service
exampleSpecs.audience: a cook learning that the difference between a calm service and a weeded one is decided at 3pm, not 7pm
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the kitchen blows ticket times and the chef pulls dishes off the menu
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cook arranges every container within one arm's reach in the order tickets fire, and the reader sees that 'least effort' was engineered hours before the first order printed
